title: rwb-comms generation request key and P5 document-create operation are not specified
source: RWB-E2-026 (v5) section 12 and 13; TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-A; context pack P6
description: The legacy story keeps the request key in an IdempotencyRepository of the document hub and writes the document row itself. After the split the document rows, files and the DocumentStored event belong to rwb-document, so the idempotency key and the request lock of AC8 and AC9 must live in rwb_comms, but no source names a rwb_comms table for them (the ownership map lists only template, merge_field and notice). The exact method, path and payload of the rwb-document create operation are also not in this work package; the P6 appendix T-A has no generated-documents endpoint.
evidence: TSD P6 T-A.1 lists API-P6-001 to API-P6-011 and none of them creates a document; the source story states the endpoint is new and recorded in an additions file; Arch v5 names document and file storage as rwb-document.
owner_role: Service owner, rwb-comms; service owner, rwb-document
proposed: Keep the request key and the request lock in a table of rwb_comms added by the V-baseline migration of the service; take the create operation from RWB-P5-E2026-CON when that contract story is written and record it in the P6 API specification.

title: Generated-documents endpoint is not in the P6 operation inventory
source: TSD P6 Communications v2 appendix T-A.1; RWB-E2-026 (v5) section 12
description: The generation endpoint is a new addition from the legacy additions file and has no API-P6-nnn ID, so it is not in the ownership map of 11 operations provided by P6. The story keeps the legacy path below the per-service base as /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/generated-documents.
evidence: Context pack P6 ownership rows: 11 REST operations provided, none of them a generation endpoint; legacy story section 12 says 'new, recorded in the additions file'.
proposed: Allocate the next API-P6-nnn ID at D1 and add the operation to the P6 API specification with the gateway-bff route.
